item.title: Nvidia launches independent probe into CEO Jensen Huang’s ties to alleged Chinese spy
item.description:
Nvidia launches independent probe into CEO Jensen Huang’s ties to alleged Chinese spy

Nvidia announced that its board has opened an independent investigation into CEO Jensen Huang’s relationship with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, who U.S. officials say was recruited by China’s Ministry of State Security to spy on the company.

🔍 Overview

  • Nvidia is investigating Jensen Huang’s relationship with a Chinese spy.
  • The investigation follows reports that Huang had a “close relationship” – later admitted as romantic in a company memo – with the Megaspeed executive.
  • Megaspeed is a customer of Nvidia and is under a Commerce Department probe for allegedly smuggling AI chips to China.

🛡️ National security context

  • Nvidia’s AI chips are viewed as crucial to the United States maintaining technological supremacy.
  • Both the Biden and Trump administrations have restricted Nvidia’s chip sales to China.
  • President Trump has loosened some restrictions but still bars sales of Nvidia’s most powerful chips to Chinese firms; the Commerce Department must approve any individual firm that handles those chips.

📋 Board response

  • The NVIDIA Board is initiating an independent investigation in light of recent reporting that Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort.
  • A committee of independent directors, assisted by outside independent counsel, will oversee the investigation.
  • The Board says it prioritizes U.S. national and economic security, which it deems paramount to the interests of NVIDIA and its shareholders.
  • While the Board has no reason to believe that national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised, the inquiry will examine all available information.

📧 Corporate statements

  • Jensen Huang fully supports the review and has committed to cooperating with it.
  • The Board has confidence in Jensen and his leadership team and will provide further updates as appropriate.
  • The New York Times reported that Huang later admitted the relationship was romantic in a memo to the company.
  • U.S. officials believe Alice Huang was feeding information directly back to Beijing.
  • There is concern about whether any insights Jensen Huang may have had about U.S. administration deliberations on AI were shared with Alice Huang and ultimately reached Beijing.

Source: Nvidia is investigating Jensen Huang’s relationship with a Chinese spy

item.title: Rep. Ro Khanna Calls for US-China Treaty to Regulate AI Risks
item.description:
Rep. Ro Khanna Calls for US-China Treaty to Regulate AI Risks

Representative Ro Khanna (D-CA) is calling for a treaty between the United States and China to prevent artificial intelligence from “wreaking havoc on the world,” citing a lack of urgency from leaders in both nations to manage the technology’s risks.

⚙️ Key details

Khanna has sent letters to the Office of the Director of National Intelligence (ODNI) and several Chinese AI companies. His requests include:

  • For the ODNI: An assessment of how the US would respond to an AI lab losing control of its bots and an evaluation of the Chinese government’s approach to catastrophic AI risks.
  • For Chinese AI Companies: Documentation regarding efforts to achieve “superintelligence” and recursive self-improvement (RSI), which is when AI systems can improve on themselves.
  • Safeguards: Information on “kill switches” and whether companies would commit to inspections by a non-governmental agency if a treaty were established.
Company Focus
DeepSeek Pursuing high-level artificial intelligence
Alibaba Pursuing high-level artificial intelligence
Moonshot AI Pursuing high-level artificial intelligence

💡 Why it matters

Khanna seeks a treaty that would ban RSI and monitor frontier AI labs, arguing that the drive for profit should not determine safety rules. He believes the US can drive these standards because many Chinese models are distilled from US models.

This move follows a meeting between President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping. While Khanna noted it was constructive that they agreed to a dialogue, he described it as “not nearly adequate” and a “branding exercise.”

🔍 Divergent Perspectives

  • Support for Treaty: Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-VT) has similarly called for a US-China AI treaty. Leading US AI companies have also called for coordination with China to slow development.
  • Skepticism: House China Committee Chair John Moolenaar (R-MI) has expressed skepticism that the Chinese government would adhere to such an agreement.
  • Executive Position: President Trump has been resistant to most agreements, stating on Truth Social that regarding “Super Intelligence (SI),” he wants to “leave it exactly where it is,” noting that this is also China’s position.

#AISafety #USChinaRelations #Superintelligence #AIRegulation

Source: Will Chinese AI companies slow down? A top House Democrat wants answers
